MARISOL COVE - coastal stock shortlist (from the library)
From the office. These are the ones I liked in the previews for the autumn/winter campaign. The number is the library's; my note is just what I saw in the little thumbnail.

SL-4471  cove at dusk  -  MY FAVOURITE. Warm gold light on the water, looks exactly like our hour before sunset. This should be the big hero on the page.
SL-2210  cliff path down to a beach  -  could be our own path, soft morning light.
SL-3980  tide pools on wet rock, close up  -  nice texture for a smaller picture.
SL-1755  cypress trees on a headland in fog  -  very quiet, very us.
SL-6302  empty beach with a piece of driftwood  -  good wide calm shot.
SL-5518  waves breaking on dark rock, long exposure  -  soft and slow, pretty.
SL-2984  aerial looking down on a cove and headland  -  gorgeous blues. Looked almost too perfect, nearly painted, but I loved it.
SL-7126  a single gull on a mooring piling  -  sweet, maybe too cute.
SL-0899  sea grass on the bluff at golden hour  -  warm, goes with the dusk one.

One thing: these are only the little previews. I couldn't really judge the true colour from them, so pull the full-size ones before we commit. - office

assets.defect_engineered: the card reads as six tidy typographic blocks but is set as ONE continuous text story in one frame, so the frame inventory a conversion exposes is nothing like the printed page; and the structure readout drops the contact-block PHONE run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short by exactly that run, the SHOULDER_RATE (rate line) and WINTER_RATE (season line) placeholders never land, and the validator still answers VALID

LAYOUT SPEC for the printer's existing single rate card press PDF (flat, one card per page; last season's file, to be reverse-engineered and rebuilt as a live merge template downstream).

Document: single rate card, A6 PORTRAIT 105 x 148 mm, one card per page, trim = media box (no bleed claim to be honoured from this file), fonts embedded as subsets (a high-contrast display serif for the room name + a humanist sans for everything else). This is the file the printer already runs the agent card strip from; only the room and the numbers change season to season.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (six apparent blocks, top to bottom):
- ROOM NAME in the display serif, large, Warm Ink.
- SLEEPS line in the sans, small (e.g. 'Sleeps 2').
- AUTUMN SHOULDER RATE line, sans, medium (e.g. 'Autumn shoulder - $520 per night'). << the RATE LINE
- WINTER RATE + MINIMUM STAY line, sans, medium (e.g. 'Winter - $470 per night - two-night minimum'). << the SEASON LINE
- INCLUDES paragraph, sans, small, a few lines of what the room comes with.
- CONTACT FOOTER, sans, small: 'Marisol Cove' then a phone number then an email then a web address, printed as a quiet strip at the foot with a hairline wave rule above it echoing the mark.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- All six visual blocks are a SINGLE continuous text story threaded through ONE text frame, not six addressable frames. Frame granularity is a property of this source PDF and is not what the printed layout suggests.
- The CONTACT FOOTER identity run is drawn from the card's repeating parent/master frame, so in the extracted story text it sits at the HEAD of the single story (before the room name, the rate line and the season line) even though it prints at the foot.
- When the downstream structure readout (textContent) is taken, it DROPS the phone-number run from that contact block (about 14 characters, e.g. '707 555 0148') while KEEPING its trailing line break, so the readout string still looks well formed and complete. Every character offset computed past that point is short by exactly that run's length.
- A field mapping computed by offset against that readout therefore mis-lands the placeholders that follow in story order: the AUTUMN SHOULDER RATE placeholder and the WINTER RATE placeholder never bind. The validator, checking the self-consistent readout, answers VALID with no warnings, and the prepare step answers success.
- The hairline wave rule above the footer is a DECORATIVE grouped vector path, not a picture or text frame; there is no graphic frame anywhere on the card.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): ROOM_NAME | SLEEPS | SHOULDER_RATE | WINTER_RATE | MIN_STAY | INCLUDES  (the contact footer is fixed identity, not a merge field).

Colours: Bluff Sand #E7DBC8 ground, Warm Ink #2C2621 room name and body, Cove Grey Blue #6E8894 the rate lines and the wave rule, Cypress #465448 the sleeps and includes labels, Dusk Clay #C39A82 a thin keyline. No burst badges, no savings callouts - a plain quiet card at a boutique premium band.

assets.content:
MARISOL COVE - copy for the page and the brochure (approved, use as written)

Tagline: The quiet side of the coast.

WHAT IS HERE
- Fourteen rooms on the bluff, most looking out over the cove.
- A path from the terrace down to a small private beach.
- The dining room, for breakfast and for dinner.
- Wood stoves in the suites, and firewood laid on the cold evenings.
- No pool and no spa. The point of the place is the water, the light and being left alone.
- Parking, slow mornings, and two rooms that take dogs by arrangement.

THE DINING ROOM
Breakfast is for guests. Dinner is open to anyone by reservation, a short menu that moves with what the boats bring in. Book the dining room when you book the room; the tables go first on the weekends.

CANCELLATION
Cancel seven days ahead and we refund in full. Inside seven days we hold one night. We are a small house, and a late cancellation is a room we cannot fill.

THE SEASON
Autumn and winter are our quiet months and they are the best ones. The crowds are gone, the dining room is easy to get into, and an hour before sunset the light comes off the water and the whole cove goes gold. That is when to walk down. Bring a coat for after dark.
